rules.title: Shops and offices with homes
rules.plain: Mission Bernal lots are for a wide range of shops, services and offices, with homes encouraged above the second story: up to one home per 600 square feet of lot area, or the nearest residential district's density if that is greater (that comparison isn't shown). Each home needs 80 square feet of private or 100 square feet of shared open space (or the nearest residential district's amount, if that's less).

rules.title: Where height is measured from
rules.plain: Height is measured from the curb at the middle of the building's street front. On a lot that slopes up from the street, only the first 10 feet back are measured from the curb, and the rest from the average ground at the two sides of each cross-section; on a lot that slopes down, the curb is used for the first 100 feet, or halfway to the street behind if that's farther.

rules.title: Housing Choice-SF
rules.plain: On lots in the Family Zoning Plan's R-4 districts, a housing project can opt into Housing Choice-SF. It may then be as tall as the second number in the R-4 height label (65 ft in 40//65-R-4), and at least 65 ft on a corner lot or a lot larger than 8,000 sq ft. Its rear yard is 18% of lot depth (at least 15 ft), with none needed at the ground floor. Open space and exposure requirements don't apply, and FAR doesn't limit its homes.

params.assumes: a project that adds homes (2 or more units, at least two-thirds residential, no other density bonus) and doesn't demolish a historic building, a hotel or a building with more than 2 rent-controlled units
params.notDrawn: the optional height bonuses (up to 30 ft), 20 ft more for 100% affordable projects, §263.20's 5 ft for tall ground floors, the 15% adjustments to other standards and the Citywide Design Standards

rules.title: Height limit
rules.plain: No part of a building may be taller than the height limit mapped for this lot's height and bulk district.

rules.title: Ground floor height
rules.plain: A shop or other non-residential ground floor must be at least 14 feet from floor to floor, or 10 feet in 40- and 50-foot height districts.

rules.title: Rear yard
rules.plain: The back 25% of the lot, and never less than 15 feet, must stay open from the lowest story with homes up; with shops on the ground floor, that's from the second story.

rules.title: Bulk limits
rules.plain: Above a height set by the lot's bulk district (the letter after the height, as in 65-A), no floor may be longer, or longer corner to corner, than the district allows.

rules.title: Floor area for non-residential uses
rules.plain: Shops, offices and other non-residential uses may have floor area up to 3.6 times the lot area; homes don't count toward this limit.

rules.title: Sidewalk setback
rules.plain: Where the sidewalk is narrower than the Better Streets Plan recommends, a lot with 50 feet or more of frontage, a corner lot or a lot next to a set-back building must set its first 15 feet of height back to widen the sidewalk; sidewalk widths aren't in this app's data.

rules.title: Taller ground floor bonus
rules.plain: A building may rise 1 foot higher for each foot of ground-floor clear ceiling height above 10 feet, or each foot its ground-floor homes are raised above the sidewalk, up to 5 feet, in 30-X, 40-X and 50-X districts (and R-4 districts with a 40, 50 or 80 foot limit). This district's table permits it "in some districts" without saying which; it isn't shown.

rules.title: Narrow streets
rules.plain: On a street or alley 40 feet wide or narrower, away from the corner, upper stories must step back at least 10 feet above a height of 1.25 times the street's width (two-story buildings are exempt), and on the south side of an east-west narrow street they must stay under a 45-degree plane from the opposite property line. Street widths aren't in this app's data, so that isn't shown.

rules.title: Cross-slope
rules.plain: Where the height limit is 65 feet or less and the street slopes along the lot's front, or the ground slopes across a lot that rises from the street, by more than 5%, a wide building is measured from several points, each covering at most 65 feet (35 to 55 on steeper slopes; on R-4 lots up to 85 feet tall, 55 to 85). It doesn't apply where §270 bulk limits apply. This view measures from one point.
